 Kenny Gainwell (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
 Gainwell has been a little more involved in recent weeks, and coach Todd Bowles recently told reporters that they are getting closer to the 1A/1B usage that they envisioned when they signed him. Gainwell will again play sidekick to Bucky Irving this week.

 Kenny Gainwell was a full participant in Thursday’s practice. 
 Gainwell never seemed in danger of missing Week 9 against the Bears, but the 27-year-old should be just fine for the Week 9 bout against the Bears. He’s coming off a monster 140-yard performance against Atlanta, but keep in mind that Tampa Bay was basically a service academy school for that game with zero completions. He’s closer to FLEX than RB2. 
 Kenny Gainwell 
 TB 
 Running Back 
 #1 
 Kenneth Gainwell (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice. 
 Gainwell played through the hip injury last week to the tune of 25 carries. He starts out the week limited, but fantasy managers should expect to see the 27-year-old to play in Week 9 against the Bears. 
 Kenny Gainwell 
 TB 
 Running Back 
 #1 
 Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said RB Kenneth Gainwell’s usage is getting closer to the “1A, 1B” usage the team envisioned when signing him. 
 Gainwell saw 25 carries in a run-heavy game against the Falcons in Week 8. Bowles said, “I think we finally got to where we’re utilizing Kenny more and more, and that’s kind of the 1A, 1B we were talking about when we first signed him.” Gainwell saw 50-percent of the snaps for the first time all season last week and now has back-to-back weeks of at least 14 carries. He is still seeing low utilization in the passing game and game script has certainly played a role in his recent role, but it is notable that Bowles mentions the Bucs envisioned a 1A/1B backfield pairing between Bucky Irving and Gainwell. Despite Bowles’ comments, fantasy managers should anticipate Irving operating with the majority of backfield touches, like he did from Weeks 1-6. We will still have to see Gainwell’s usage in a more neutral game script to feel confident about him as a fantasy option moving forward. 
 Kenny Gainwell 
 TB 
 Running Back 
 #1 
 Kenneth Gainwell rushed 25 times for 140 yards in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons. 
 Bucky Irving gave the Bucs a 16-0 lead entering the fourth quarter and passed the baton to Gainwell, who racked up 18 carries in the final frame. Irving only touched the ball once over the final 15 minutes. Gainwell’s late-game dominance got him up to career-highs in carries and yards. He also managed a season-high 14 attempts under similar circumstances last week. Unfortunately for Gainwell, the Bucs aren’t likely to be playing with a big lead in Week 9 against the Bears. Gainwell will return to the RB3/4 border next week.

 Running Back 
 #1 
 Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Falcons. 
 Right tackle Luke Goedeke is also active. Gainwell will continue mixing in behind Bucky Irving this week. He has yet to hit a dozen fantasy points in a game this year and there’s no reason to expect that to change anytime soon. Gainwell is a low-end RB4 for Week 8. Inactive for the Bucs are DL DeMonte Capehart, WR Emeka Egbuka, CB Ayden Garnes, OT Luke Haggard, and OG Billy Schrauth. 
 Kenny Gainwell 
 TB 
 Running Back 
 #1 
 ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is “good to go” for Week 8 against the Falcons. 
 Week 7 was Gainwell’s first game with more than seven touches all year. He handled 14 opportunities, all of which were carries, and they came in a 30-point blowout win over the Panthers. Unless the Bucs stay hot and roll over the Falcons, expect Gainwell’s touch total to return to the single digits. He is barely in the RB4 mix for Week 8.

 Kenny Gainwell (hip) is questionable for Tampa’s Week 8 game against Atlanta. 
 His absence would free up more work for Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker. Presumably Gainwell will play after logging a full practice on Friday. Either way, with an injury also nipping at him, he’s an unenviable FLEX option at best against the Falcons.

 Running Back 
 #1 
 Kenneth Gainwell (hip) returned to practice Thursday. 
 Gainwell missed Wednesday’s session with the hip issue. He will likely be listed as limited today, but that still puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Falcons. Gainwell racked up 14 carries in a blowout win over the Panthers last week, but that hasn’t been the norm for him. Gainwell is averaging 6.4 touches per game and has topped out at three receptions in a week. He is buried in the RB4 ranks for Week 8. 
 Kenny Gainwell 
 TB 
 Running Back 
 #1 
 Kenneth Gainwell (hip) did not practice Wednesday. 
 Gainwell suffered the hip injury while logging a season-high 14 rush attempts in Week 7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers and racked up 49 carries as a team. Bucky Irving would be in line for more work on passing downs if Gainwell is out for Week 8. Sean Tucker could also see an uptick in snaps, though his normal role has very little overlap with what Gainwell does. Per usual, Irving looks like a high-end RB2 this week. 
 Kenny Gainwell 
 TB 
 Running Back 
 #1 
 Kenneth Gainwell rushed 14 times for 88 yards in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers. 
 Gainwell was not targeted in the passing game, but that’s because Baker Mayfield attempted only 11 throws. That in turn was due to the fact that Tampa road paved Carolina on the ground as the Panthers committed four turnovers. It’s why Gainwell rushed for a season-high 88 yards after never perviously reaching 20. He was still out-carried 24-14 by Bucky Irving, who found the end zone twice as Sean Tucker hit pay dirt once. We are sure this is a formula the Bucs would like to replicate moving forward, but it is not going to be doable most of the time. It does at least make Gainwell a slightly more realistic FLEX option heading into Week 8 against the Falcons.

 Jadarian Price rushed nine times for 24 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 54 yards on four receptions.
 Price’s 13 opportunities lagged the 18 of Zach Charbonnet in what is developing into a true 60-40 split between him and the veteran, and while the 54 yards through the air were impressive, Price appears to need consistent aerial production to sustain his fantasy value moving forward while playing on the wrong side of a timeshare. Hopefully he can improve upon the modest 2.7 yards per carry he notched against the Cardinals when the Seahawks take on the sliding Raiders in Week 10.
 -  Mark Garcia

 Zach Charbonnet rushed 16 times for 77 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding nine yards on one reception.
 Charbonnet served as the clear lead back against an inferior Cardinals team, handling 16 carries and two targets to the nine carries and four targets of rookie Jadarian Price. The roughly 60-40 split between the two is likely closer to what to expect for the remainder of the season now that Charbonnet has another game under his belt coming off the 2025 torn ACL. The fantasy returns could be much greater against arguably the worst defense in the league at present, with Charbonnet inching closer to weekly FLEX status ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Raiders.

 Dylan Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints, adding three catches for 27 yards.
 Per usual, Sampson did the bulk of his damage through the air, especially in PPR leagues. He saw six targets compared to just one for Quinshon Judkins. Sampson’s role is good for a few weekly PPR points, but his lack of rushing production makes a ceiling outcome almost impossible. He’ll be a viable RB4 fantasy option when the Browns take on the Texans next week.

 The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that the Colts informed Daniel Jones that they are not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline.
 Jones successfully returned from last year’s season-ending Achilles tendon rupture, but his play has been negatively impacted by it. With two young quarterbacks on the roster, it would seemingly make sense to trade Jones to get an extended look at either Riley Leonard and/or Anthony Richardson. Apparently, the Colts disagree. We have no way of knowing whether Pelissero’s report is a hardball negotiation tactic by the Colts’ front office, but we will have an answer to that question in the next couple of days.
 -  Nic Bodiford

 Christian Watson caught 7-of-8 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
 Watson and fellow receiver Matthew Golden combined to catch 14 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, as both receivers attacked downfield at will against an overmatched Patriots secondary. Watson saw four of his seven receptions go for 20-plus yards, and found the end zone on a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter, one play after the Packers’ defense forced a turnover. Watson has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has four games of 100-plus-yard performances on his resumé this season. He draws a tough Week 10 matchup against the Vikings and will be in the mix as a high-end WR2.
 -  Zachary Krueger

 Quinshon Judkins rushed 15 times for 43 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
 Judkins was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage constantly, resulting in a dreadful yards per carry of 2.9. This was particularly painful for fantasy managers when he got near the end zone. Judkins was stuffed from the one- and three-yard line on separate drives. He also ceded receiving work to Dylan Sampson. Judkins was targeted once while Sampson saw six opportunities through the air. Without receiving work to buoy his poor rushing days, Judkins is tumbling down the RB2 ranks. He’ll be on the RB2/3 border for his Week 10 matchup with the Texans. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Drew Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 17-3, Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 16 yards on five carries.
 Lock appeared to suffer discomfort in the third quarter following an incomplete pass attempt, holding his side or oblique and grimacing in pain as he made his way to sideline. He would get checked in the medical tent but returned without missing a down. Lock looked poised in the pocket and in control of the offense throughout, leaning on his alpha wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba early before the team went into preservation mode with a sizable lead in the second half. Lock could be looking at another start or two, pending the length of recovery from a cracked rib for Sam Darnold. His next start will come against arguably the worst defense in the league in the Raiders in Week 10, where Lock will border streamer status in deeper leagues.
 -  Mark Garcia 
 Recap

 Drake Maye 
 NE

 Drake Maye completed 21-of-38 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27, Week 9 loss to the Packers.
 Maye’s three first-half interceptions but the Patriots in the hole early, but the defenses’ inability to limit explosive plays also didn’t do them any favors. The Patriots saw three of their first six drives end in interceptions, but Maye did what he could to keep the game within reach. He completed his first touchdown pass of the day to Rhamondre Stevenson, who broke free down field for the 30-yard score in the second quarter. and on the following drive, Maye would complete passes of 19 and 28 yards to set up Efton Chism for an eight-yard touchdown with less than three minutes to go in the half. His third and final touchdown would come on a 22-yard pass to Mack Hollins, but Maye and the Patriots were under duress all afternoon and struggled to keep up with a Packers offense that didn’t slow down until it pulled it’s starters late in the fourth quarter. Maye also took four sacks in this one and has now been sacked nine times in his last three games. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Lions in Munich.
 -  Zachary Krueger 
 Recap

 Jordan Love

 Quarterback

 Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots.
 As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.
 -  Zachary Krueger
